  MINUTES
  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  July 6, 2021
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:05 p.m., on Tuesday, July 6, 2021 the Alhambra City Council met in Council
Chambers and via video conference.

PRESENT via video conference:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
PRESENT:  LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present physically, via teleconference, and via video conference: City Manager
Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia, City Clerk Myles, Director of
Community Development Ho

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-87

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956
of the Government Code of the State of California.

CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING

1.  APPLICATIONS FOR VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP TT 74194, RESIDENTIAL
  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT RP-17-7, CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CU-17-9
  AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE PROPOSED
  VILLAGES AT THE ALHAMBRA PROJECT (PROJECT) WITH 294 NEW, FOR-SALE,
  RESIDENTIAL DWELLING UNITS IN FIVE-STORY STACKED FLAT AND
  TOWNHOME CONFIGURATIONS; 545 NEW RENTAL APARTMENTS IN FIVE-STORY
  STACKED FLAT CONFIGURATIONS; AND UP TO 4,347 TOTAL PARKING SPACES
  TO ACCOMMODATE ALL NEW USES. IT IS EXPECTED THAT IF THE PROJECT IS
  APPROVED THE APPLICANT WILL IMPLEMENT A PARKING REDUCTION
  PURSUANT TO ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.52.060. THE PROJECT
  SITE IS LOCATED IN THE PO (PROFESSIONAL OFFICE) ZONE. AN
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT HAS BEEN PREPARED FOR THE PROJECT
  AND WILL ALSO BE CONSIDERED WITH THE PROJECT ALONG WITH A POSSIBLE
  STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS – F2M17-50, N2M20-163

  At the June 17th Special City Council meeting, the Council received verbal and written
  comments in support and in opposition to the proposed project and discussed the project
  further. Following their discussion, the Council continued the item to this evening. Since
  the Council’s last meeting, the LOS analysis and Air Quality have been completed and
  posted on the website. The VMT analysis memo has been updated for the revised 790-
  unit project and posted on the website. These documents are also attached to the July 6,

  1
7-6-21
   2021 report by the Director of Community Development. The Applicant has also submitted
  a draft development agreement incorporating terms negotiated by the two Council Sub-
  Committees for the Council’s consideration. This draft development agreement was also
  attached to the July 6, 2021 report by the Director of Community Development.

  Discussion: Mayor LEE requested information regarding the pending water quality
  report from the Regional Water Quality Control Board. City Manager BINNQUIST stated
  that the report had not yet been provided to staff for presentation to Council. Mayor LEE
  requested that Council consider a motion to continue the public hearing to another date.
  Councilmember PÉREZ supported continuing the meeting given the importance of the
  report from the Regional Water Quality Control Board and gave an appropriate motion.
  Council went on to continue discussion of the date for the next meeting with Ms.
  BINNQUIST and Megan MOLOUGHNEY, representing The Ratkovich Company.
  Alexander DeGood, counsel to the Applicant, discussed their preference for Council to
  not delay the hearing for the Water Quality Report, since it would not provide any new
  significant insight into the project at this stage. Mayor LEE seconded Ms. Pérez’s motion
  to continue the meeting, and reiterated the need for Council to review the water quality
  report addressing potential contamination of the site.

  Councilmember MALONEY and Director of Community Development HO discussed
  staff’s need for direction from Council before continuing discussion with the Applicant.
  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. PÉREZ continued to discuss the
  possibility of continuing the meeting to review the forthcoming report from the Regional
  Water Quality Control Board. Ms. PÉREZ and City Attorney MONTES discussed the
  process after Council closes the Public Hearing and provides direction to staff. Mr.
  MONTES explained the City’s process, the next steps of Council, the continued work
  between staff and the applicant, and the potential timeline for this to be accomplished. Mr.
  MALONEY supported the motion to continue the meeting.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. MALONEY discussed the need for staff to continue to
  refine the Development Agreement based on previous comments from Council and the
  report from the Subcommittee meetings. Councilmember MAZA and Mr. MONTES
  discussed potential outcomes of the Water Quality Report as it might affect the
  Development Agreement. Mr. MAZA supported the motion to continue the meeting.

  Council went on to discuss dates to continue the meeting with Ms. BINNQUIST. Ms.
  PÉREZ amended her motion to continue the hearing open to August 10, 2021 at 6:00
  p.m. Ms. LEE confirmed that Council would like staff to continue to finalize the
  Development Agreement for presentation at the August 10, 2021 meeting. Mr. MONTES
  clarified that the majority of issues Council identified in previous meetings as well as the
  Subcommittee meetings would be accounted for in the revisions to the Development
  Agreement, however additional comments could be made at the next meeting when staff
  would either prepare approval or denial documents based on Council’s decision.

  Ms. PÉREZ further discussed the Subcommittee meetings and recent requests made with
  regards to additional affordable housing accommodations.

  Action Taken:  City Council continued the hearing open to August 10, 2021 at 6:00
  p.m., and deferred taking any additional public testimony until that date, when it was
  anticipated additional information would be available.

  2
7-6-21
   Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

ADJOURNMENT: At 6:06 p.m., there being no further business for the Council to transact, the
Mayor, with the consent of the City Council, adjourned their meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
  by
